archetypes.name: downstream-consumer-sweep
archetypes.rationale: Plan scopes to 8 files but the OOS format contract touches additional consumers (parse-input.sh, oos-pipeline, Step 9a.1 batch builder) that could remain broken or break under producer renumbering; existing test fixtures may assert specific OOS ids that shift after monotonic renumbering.
archetypes.prompt_body: Search the codebase for all files that parse or match `### OOS_` or `### FINDING.*OUT_OF_SCOPE` headers beyond the 8 scope files — pay particular attention to `skills/issue/scripts/parse-input.sh`, any Step 9a.1 batch-builder script, and `oos-pipeline.md`. Verify the plan's claim that these consumers are safe because producer normalization happens upstream, and confirm no out-of-scope consumer can ever see a legacy-format header. Inspect existing test fixtures in the 8 scope files for hard-coded `### OOS_N:` id values (e.g. `OOS_1`, `OOS_2`) that the plan's monotonic renumbering would silently change, breaking those assertions. Check whether the `tally-code-votes.md` and `oos-disposition-gate.md` doc updates cover the full set of consumers that have behavioral expectations about OOS header format. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: awk-python-regex-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan extends awk and Python regexes independently; awk checks existence of `[OUT_OF_SCOPE]` anywhere on the line via index() while Python anchors the tag immediately after the colon+space, creating silent divergence for real-world header shapes like `### FINDING_1: Some Title [OUT_OF_SCOPE]`.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the proposed awk block-start extension (`$0 ~ /^###[[:space:]]+FINDING_[0-9]+:/ && index($0, "[OUT_OF_SCOPE]")`) with the Python `_OOS_HEADER_RE` extension (`^###\s+(?:OOS_|FINDING_\d+:\s*\[OUT_OF_SCOPE\])`) for semantic equivalence on all realistic header shapes — including a tag appearing after a title (`### FINDING_1: Some Title [OUT_OF_SCOPE]`), extra whitespace between the colon and the tag, and a bare `### FINDING_1: [OUT_OF_SCOPE]` with no title text. Verify that the Python `_count_non_security` file-level guard (uses `_OOS_HEADER_RE.search(text)` before the per-line loop) correctly returns non-zero when the file contains only FINDING-tagged headers, given the regex anchoring interacts with `re.MULTILINE`. Confirm the security-exclusion sub-rule fires identically in both the awk (`focus-area: security` in-block check) and the Python path for a FINDING-tagged OOS block that also carries a security focus-area. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
